t: You're at Southwark Cathedral, close to London Bridge on the south bank of the Thames. Christians have worshipped on this spot for more than a thousand years, though it only became a cathedral in 1905. Its burials read like a roll call of the Elizabethan and Jacobean stage. The playwrights John Fletcher and Philip Massinger are buried here, as is Philip Henslowe, the theatre entrepreneur whose diary tells us so much about the period. The medieval poet John Gower is here too. So is Lancelot Andrewes, who oversaw the King James Bible, and the American actor Sam Wanamaker.
